International Media Support (IMS) is an international non-profit organisation working across multiple continents, with its head quarters in Copenhagen in Denmark and regional offices around the world. IMS’ goal is to contribute to a vibrant and inclusive civic space where the media induces actions that further human rights, accountability and social, political and cultural change. As part of this, IMS’ goal is to have public interest media reach relevant audiences so that they can discuss, share and act on this content, and to have media and civic/civil groups and organisations to collaborate to bring about this change.
IMS was established 2001 with the mission to provide rapid and flexible assistance to media in conflict countries around the world. IMS has thereafter expanded their mission to support media in countries undergoing political transition, in emerging democracies and in countries with repressive and autocratic regimes. IMS supports local media organisations to strengthen their capacity to provide conflict sensitive, gender balanced, professional and reliable information to people. They support journalism that is ethical, independent, critical and of public interest and to make it accessible to all sections of society including marginalised groups. Currently IMS works in over 20 countries in five regions – MENA, Africa, Asia, Latin America and Europe.
IMS has submitted a proposal to Sida for Core funding for implementing the IMS Strategy 2020-2023 with 30 MSEK (10m SEK annually 2021-2023). The strategy aims to reach the most vulnerable populations in repressive and conflict affected countries/regions by ensuring that members of the public can access, participate and be fairly portrayed by the media, regardless of people’s genders, identities and socio-economic circumstances. Protect media workers of all genders from risks and threats that may prevent them from producing and distributing public interest content. Challenge disinformation and hate speech. Advocate for laws and policies that protect free expression and access to information, as well as promote transparent and accountable self-regulation of content. IMS is not only striving to develop good journalism for the sake of merely having good journalism, but are supporting journalism that has the potential and the intent to bring positive change, social, political or cultural change.

International Media Support (IMS) är en internationell icke-vinstdrivande organisation som har sitt huvudkontor i Danmark och ett antal regionala kontor runtom i världen. IMS övergripande målsättning är att bidra till en levande och inkluderande samhällsdebatt där medier, genom sin rapportering, bidrar till förbättringar i samhället och som stärker de mänskliga rättigheterna, ansvarstagande, samt social, politisk och kulturell förändring. IMS arbetar med att stötta utvecklingen av oberoende journalistik och medier att nå ut med information till relevant publik/grupper så att de i sin tur kan diskutera, dela informationen och agera på innehållet, samt för att media och medborgerliga/ civila grupper och organisationer ska samarbeta för att åstadkomma denna förändring.
IMS har sedan 2001 arbetat med att erbjuda snabbt och flexibelt stöd till medier i konfliktdrabbade områden. IMS har sedan dess utökat sin verksamhet till att stötta medier i länder som präglas av förtryck, politisk instabilitet, auktoritärt styre och instabil demokrati. IMS stödjer lokala medier att utveckla och stärka sin kapacitet för att nå ut med faktagranskad, oberoende, genderbalanserad och relevant information till människor som lever i repressiva miljöer och konfliktområden. IMS verkar för etisk, oberoende och granskande journalistik som är av allmänt intresse med betoning på att informationen ska nå alla delar av samhället, inklusive marginaliserade grupper. IMS arbetar globalt och bedriver idag verksamhet i över 20 länder utspridda på fem kontinenter - MENA, Afrika, Asien, Latinamerika och Europa.
IMS har inkommit med en ansökan till Sida om kärnstöd för att implementera IMS Strategi 2020-2023 med 30 MSEK för perioden 2021-2023 (10 MSEK per år). Strategin syftar till att nå de mest utsatta befolkningarna i repressiva och konfliktdrabbade länder/ regioner genom att säkerställa att allmänheten kan få tillgång oberoende information, möjligheter till delaktighet och rättvis representation i medier, oavsett kön, identitet eller socio-ekonomiska omständigheter. Vidare har strategin som mål att öka skyddet för journalister och mediaarbetare av alla kön, motverka desinformation och hatpropaganda samt verka för lagar och policyer som skyddar yttrandefriheten och tillgången till information.

sector.narrative: Media and free flow of information

description.narrative:
During the reporting period IMS worked with 135 strategic partners and 98activity partners. Partners were supported by IMS 35 programmes operating in Africa, Asia, Eastern Europe, the Middle East and Northern Africa and around the globe via IMS global advocacy and rapid response interventions. Results recorded for 2022 show the highest concentration of results in the outcome area related to public interest content and media, including the production and distribution of public interest content through core support and expert mentoring and advising, with focuses on indepth and investigative journalism, documentary film and collaboration with hyperlocal media that have contributed to social, political or cultural changes in some of the most challenged parts of the world.
19,500 media workers were supported by various safety measures related to prevention, protection and prosecution. Results are recorded from work on safety mechanisms in ten countries and the involvement of various international stakeholders on relevant safety frameworks and measures. IMS reports on media partners supporting journalists and media workers in continuing their work despite operating in adverse and repressive environments.IMS reports on of media partners facilitating and enabling participation in public debates and examples of audiences using public interest media content to take concrete action. Results compiled provide more than fifty examples in which media, as the key stakeholders, have been able to hold duty bearers to account and expose corruption, abuses of power and the consequences of inequality, in many cases through close collaborations with civil society actors.
In the 2022 Annual report IMS comes out strongly as a catalyst for a locally led media sector development, and IMS contribution is ascribed as crucial for progress and achievements and in some cases as critical for medias continued existence and ability to produce public interest content, including from exile. IMS also reports on a pattern across recorded results that are directly linked to collaborative and networking actions. Examples can be seen in the Pakistan and Somalia programmes, as well as the work related the marking the anniversary of the UN Plan of Action on the Safety of Journalists and the Issue of Impunity.
IMS and partners have built and strengthened advocacy alliances and coalition in programme countries and on a global level that involve not just media and media support organisations but also civic organisations and movements with an interest in creating an open and inclusive civic space particularly those representing the interests of women and marginalised sections of society. Significant outcomes can be seen in countries such as Pakistan, the Philippines and Somalia, which are the results of several years of concerted effort in most cases, building on coordinated work in coalitions or alliances across sectors and with a multitude of stakeholders. A third of the recorded outcomes include work on safety mechanisms on national and global levels and demonstrate how IMS works with a multipronged approach that promotes the three Ps (prevention, protection and prosecution). IMS has engaged and influenced numerous international key stakeholders to act and address issues on the safety of journalists. As an example: IMS played a leading role in the Global Forum for Media Development (GFMD) subgroup on safety and personal protective equipment (PPE) discussed the lack of coordination related to the distribution of PPE to journalist in Ukraine. As a result, an agreement on a common standard was reached, addressing the quality of some of the PPE and the lack of PPE in smaller sizes (jeopardising the safety of journalists in Ukraine, especially women journalists).
Rapid Response During 2022 IMS employed its Rapid Response (RR) mechanism to address urgent crises and emerging opportunities by supporting interventions in the following countries: Mozambique, Philippines, Sri Lanka, Syria, Thailand, Turkey, Ukraine and some activities in neighbouring countries. Interventions and activities spanned accountability journalism (Phillipines and Mozambique), emergency response (Ukraine, Turkey, Syria), training (Thailand, Phillipines), legal assistance, content production following periods of unrest and relocation of media (Syria). While these interventions are of shortterm character to address immediate needs, strategic, longterm perspectives are integrated into the interventions.
Gender equality IMS work on gender equality is based on both the institutional strategy and the 2021 strategy on gender equality. In 2022, IMS supported 124 gender specific activities, a 20 percent increase since 2020. Most results fall under outcome area 1 on public interest media. Activities cover training and mentoring of women content producers, but it is also noticeable that more activities focus on producing content on gender issues or with feminist perspectives. In 2022 IMS partner activities on gendered disinformation have appeared for the first time.
